scope: Selected works beyond the survey April 2026 cutoff; dates follow arXiv v1 submission histories or explicitly identified official release announcements and are not independent proof of first public availability. This is an expert-curated update, not an exhaustive search.

classification.Dataset: Training corpora, evaluation data, competitive archives, and explicitly labeled data-scaling studies. Announced resources are distinguished from downloadable releases.
classification.Model: Learned policies and game world models; simulators and neural renderers are distinguished from policies that select actions.
classification.Harness: Deployment-time perception, planning, memory, control, tool use, and adaptation around a model. Model-weight updates are identified separately.
classification.Benchmark: Capability targets and declared evaluation protocols. Recorded-video understanding is distinguished from closed-loop gameplay.

entries.name: Matrix-Game 4.0
entries.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
entries.date_basis: Official repository release news is October 15; repository news reports technical report October 16; arXiv v1 submitted October 20.

entries.summary: Combines an executable game engine, coding-agent orchestration, and a trained causal video renderer for low-latency playable shooter and driving worlds.

entries.notes: The engine owns persistent state and game rules; the video model renders low-poly proxies. Related world-generation infrastructure, not an autonomous native-action game-playing policy. A secondary Harness tag reflects the executable engine and coding agent; do not call it a fully learned WAM. Released assets are not a training dataset release.

entries.release_status: Official benchmark methodology and launch report public; no dedicated author-linked code repository or standalone trajectory corpus verified.
entries.notes: Uses Inspect ReAct with screenshots, persistent notes across context compaction, and wiki-restricted search. The earlier epoch.ai URL refers to this same benchmark.
